newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen ends up on U.S. job data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen ends up on U.S. job data.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures ended on a firmer note on Monday following the weaker than expected U.S. August employment data, dealers said.
Although weaker than expected, the U.S. job data released on Friday, triggered market fears that the U.S. interest rates might be hiked in the next Federal Open Market Committee meet on September 24.

After soaring eight ticks from its previous CME close at 99.07, March Euroyen settled near its intraday high, at 99.12. Turnover was light at 7,765 lots. December ended at 99.29 against 99.26 previously.
The December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures climbed 64 ticks to end at 121.28 on a turnover of 545 lots.

Dealers, baffled by the firm JGBs, said the futures could be fuelled by strong demand for cash bonds. They said JGBs could also have received a further boost from a rise in the U.S. treasury bonds after the U.S. job data on Friday.

Dealers added the market was also underpinned by Japanese election talks. They also awaited the release of Japan's July machinery orders data due on September 10 for a clearer indication of the economy.

Some analysts expected the July private machinery orders, excluding ships and the electric power industry, to be up 8.5 percent month on month and up 16.5 percent year on year following a 3.2 percent year on year rise in June 1996.
March Eurodollars ended at 93.78 against its IMM close at 93.76. Turnover was light, at 9,010 lots.
